title: Schema lockdown: JSON-mode enforcement and constrained-decoding test harness
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a hardened implementation and test suite to enforce JSON-mode outputs for the Core API. Goals: (1) provide an opt-in strict JSON mode that rejects/flags non-conforming tokens early, (2) implement constrained decoding hooks that map model probabilities to schema-aware token masks, and (3) ship end-to-end schema adherence tests that cover streaming, function/tool-calling interactions, and backward compatibility via a compatibility layer. This ticket covers design decisions, a minimal runtime shim, unit+integration tests, and a rollout plan with feature flags and observability. The feature must be compatible with streaming responses and function calling: when json_mode is enabled, the runtime should prefer structured output enforcement but still allow function calls when explicitly requested.
acceptance_criteria: API: POST /v1/responses accepts 'json_mode': 'strict' and returns 4xx with error_code 'json_conformance' for responses that cannot be coerced into the provided schema
Constrained decoding: runtime exposes a token_mask callback used by the model engine; masks reduce allowed next tokens to schema-compatible tokens during generation
Streaming: chunked responses remain valid JSON fragments; client can reconstruct final JSON without needing post-hoc parsing heuristics

Function-calling compatibility: when a function signature is provided and json_mode is enabled, priority rules are documented and tests demonstrate correct selection between structured output and function call modes
Automated tests: unit tests for decoder masking, integration tests against representative models, and fuzz tests that run 10k prompt variations within CI
Observability: telemetry emits 'json_mode.success'/'json_mode.failure' metrics and example failure traces to the console dashboard
Performance: p50 latency regression < 10% for typical small-response workloads when json_mode is active (documented in performance runbook)
implementation_notes: Design a JSON canonicalizer that normalizes whitespace, ordering (where schema allows), and uses deterministic escaping to compare partial streams

Implement token_mask generator from JSON Schema: walk schema to produce allowable tokens at each generation step (supports string enums, number formats, object keys and structural tokens '{', '}', '[', ']', ':', ',')
Fallback behavior: if strict mode cannot produce conforming output within token budget, runtime should abort with structured error instead of returning malformed JSON

Streaming strategy: emit 'json_preface' token boundary and incremental valid fragments; avoid sending final '}' until complete; include a final 'json_footer' verification signature for integrity checks

Function-calling interaction: add config flag 'prefer_function_calls' with defined precedence. Default: if functions present and model returns a full function call JSON object consistent with schema, treat as function call result; otherwise, enforce structured output
Compatibility layer: provide 'compat.v1' that accepts older non-strict responses and attempts best-effort auto-coercion for legacy clients (logs mismatches)
Library hooks: expose a small public helper in the SDK (node/python) to reconstruct streamed structured outputs and surface schema errors to the caller
tradeoffs: Strict enforcement reduces developer confusion and downstream parsing errors but increases the chance of generation aborts and higher token consumption due to constrained decoding
Token masking is model-architecture-dependent: best results on transformer decoders with vocabulary-aware masking; older models may still produce malformed output requiring post-processing
Streaming valid-json fragments increases complexity and slightly increases bandwidth due to preface/footer markers
Compatibility layer slows rollout but preserves customer experience for legacy clients — must be behind feature flag
test_plan: Unit tests: token_mask generator correctness for 50 canonical schema patterns (enums, nested objects, arrays, optional fields)
Integration: end-to-end tests against small/medium open models (llama2/opt variants) verifying full JSON reconstruction from streaming responses
Fuzzing: CI job runs 10k synthetic prompts with randomized schemas and asserts either conforming output or documented failure codes
Perf: synthetic benchmark comparing p50/p95 latency and token usage with json_mode on vs off across 3 sequence-length profiles
Regression: add nightly job that replays customer-mimic prompt set and alerts if json_mode failure rate > 0.5%
Manual review: design/PM to review SDK helper ergonomics and error messages (UX round)
rollout_plan: Feature gated by 'json_mode.strict' on account level. Start with internal dogfood org for 48 hours
Stage 1: internal teams and select customer beta (5 customers) — monitor telemetry for failures and latency impact
Stage 2: opt-in public beta (all free-tier) after addressing initial bugs
Stage 3: on-by-default for new API keys with clear migration notes; legacy keys remain under compat.v1 layer
Rollback strategy: flip feature flag and allow in-flight requests to finish; run quick revert tests to validate compatibility
dependencies: PM-420 (schema registry and canonical schema formats)
DES-224 (SDK helper UX and error copy)
